items.title: The Bursting of the Tel Aviv Bubble
items.author: Erik Marmor / Getty
items.summary: N o one talks about the left in Israel anymore. The label itself is essentially a curse word, something spat out by an angry taxi driver after he’s swerved around a guy on a scooter. A measly 12 to 15 percent of Israelis identify as such. But democracy has a much better reputation, at least in cosmopolitan, beachy Tel Aviv, which is maybe why the leftmost party running for parliament in this week’s election gave itself the name the Democrats. A liberal ethos lives here, alongside excellent coffee, delicious salads, and fashion boutiques. The city has been the epicenter of protest against Benjamin Netanyahu’s government over the past four years. Itamar Ben-Gvir, Netanyahu’s far-right interior minister, has taken to calling it “the state of Tel Aviv,” and its population of tech workers, baristas, and academics “anarchists”—enemies whose openness threatens the purer Jewish state he dreams about. The state of Tel Aviv, not exactly an inaccurate sobriquet, girded itself for the election this week and then got battered. The results can’t be called anything other than inconclusive. items.title: Why Halloween Isn’t Just for Kids
items.author: Andrea Folignoli / 500px / Getty
items.summary: This is an edition of The Wonder Reader, a newsletter in which our editors recommend a set of stories to spark your curiosity and fill you with delight. Sign up here to get it every Saturday morning. Children rarely need an excuse to be silly. They invent games, dress up on a random Tuesday, and find endless amusement in things that might seem mundane to grown-ups. But somewhere along the way, that kind of uninhibited fun becomes harder to come by. Free time for adults is often filled with plans and obligations, and even leisure can start to feel like something we ought to be doing productively. Halloween offers a welcome exception. For one night, adults can put on ridiculous costumes, eat too much candy, and lean into the absurdity. In a 2022 essay for The Atlantic , Faith Hill argued that the holiday’s childishness is precisely what makes it so valuable to grown-ups. Although traditions have changed over time—widespread mischief and juvenile pranks have largely mellowed out, supplanted by trick-or-treating and bar crawls—what remains central to the night’s celebration is the freeing sense that you can do something simply for the pleasure of it, even if that means looking a little

items.title: The Election Lies Are Already Starting on X
items.author: Illustration by Adam Maida / The Atlantic
items.summary: Last weekend, Chaya Raichik, the popular right-wing influencer who goes by Libs of TikTok, made an ominous claim to her nearly 5 million followers on X. “In Minnesota, the USPS offices are inside mosques,” she wrote. “The people who handle mail-in ballots.. What are we doing America.” She reshared a 28-minute-long video of a man circling a brick building in Plymouth, Minnesota, and accosting postal workers inside. “It’s the Islamification of the United States,” the man says. “And we have to stop it.” Almost everything about Raichik’s post is misleading. The post office is not “inside” a mosque; they are housed in different sections of the same building. And there’s no reason to believe that the shared real estate has anything to do with the integrity of elections. In situations like this, X’s crowdsourced fact-checking feature, called “Community Notes,” is supposed to help correct the record. Users propose disclaimers for popular posts they believe are inaccurate, and if other users agree, the disclaimer gets attached to the post. items.title: Buoyed by shifting political winds, ‘Deport!’ is the new ‘Go back where you come from’ echoed by racists | Ghassan Hage
items.author: Ghassan Hage
items.summary: ‘Deport!’ oozes an entirely different sense of power – one where the racist imagines they can call upon the state to act on their behalf There is a rise in racist rhetoric surrounding deportation. This is clearly influenced by the increased use of deportation against immigrants and asylum seekers worldwide, particularly in the United States. But my concern here is not so much the governmental practice itself as the racist language that it has helped disseminate and legitimise: I write something on X, and some random racist who dislikes what I wrote decides that because my name is Ghassan Hage I must be a potentially deportable subject and simply writes “deport” as a comment. Nasser Mashni, the president of the Australia Palestine Advocacy Network, notes in Crikey that “deport” is “the comment most often left on anything I post”.

items.summary: Fortune is not favouring Pierre Sage. Just when the Crystal Palace manager needed a positive result, Jean-Philippe Mateta’s early red card condemned his side to a third straight defeat in the league, leaving their manager’s position hanging by a thread. Goals from Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke ensured that Tottenham recorded a third successive victory for the first time in 616 days as they moved into the top half of the table. To put that into context, Spurs have had three full-time managers since then, so it was no wonder that Roberto De Zerbi looked so pleased at full time.

At 59 I thought to myself, “surely there’s got to be a little bit more love that I could give in my life”. But I was also keenly aware that not many people find romance organically these days. I gave Bumble a go, had some pretty average dates and thought it wasn’t for me, but I decided to give it one last shot. It was Kev’s smile and his eyes that caught my attention. His profile said travel was really important to him, which gave me a bit of a laugh because I have huge anxiety issues around holidaying of any sort. We exchanged a few texts and decided to arrange a date. It was nothing fancy, just a few drinks at a bar in a bayside suburb of Melbourne.

items.author: Marina Dunbar
items.summary: Ruling ‘with prejudice’ means US president may not amend or refile his lawsuit over his alleged birthday letter to Jeffrey Epstein A US judge dismissed Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal with prejudice on Saturday, according to a court filing, bringing an end to his legal challenge over the newspaper’s reporting on his alleged birthday letter to Jeffrey Epstein. The decision follows an earlier dismissal in April that had allowed Trump to revise his complaint. As of Saturday, the case is dismissed with prejudice, meaning the lawsuit cannot be amended or refiled.

items.title: Hera Probe Sees Asteroid Pair Separately for First Time
items.author: Laurence Tognetti, MSc
items.summary: Planetary defense is a growing concern among the scientific community, as efforts have been made to design and implement missions meant to deflect incoming threats to the Earth well in advance. In 2022, NASA intentionally collided the Double Asteroid Redirection test (DART) planetary defense spacecraft into the smaller asteroid of the binary asteroid, Didymos and Dimorphos, with the latter being the smaller one. While the goal was to ascertain if deflecting an asteroid is feasible, how did this influence the geological characteristics of Dimorphos, and what can it teach us about planetary defense missions?

items.title: Space Outposts Beyond the Moon May Rely on Planetary AI
items.author: Laurence Tognetti, MSc
items.summary: NASA plans to return astronauts to the lunar surface in 2028 for the first time since Apollo 17 in 1972. But the famed agency has no intention of stopping there, as they plan to establish a permanent human presence on the Moon through a slow and meticulous process involving power, resource extraction, and habitat technologies. However, with the soaring use of artificial intelligence (AI) in our everyday lives, how could this emerging technology be used to identify new landing sites for future outposts on the Moon and possibly Mars?

items.title: Will Melania Trump save Ukraine?
items.author: Kelli Wessinger
items.summary: Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump arrive for the 80th session of the UN General Assembly in New York City on September 23, 2025. | Alexi J. Rosenfeld/Getty Images In the last month or so, President Donald Trump’s on-again-off-again relationship with Ukraine — which has ranged from kicking Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy out of the White House in early 2025 to promising new air defense missiles this summer — has once again run cold . Trump has excoriated Zelenskyy for successful Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil and gas infrastructure , called for Zelenskyy’s ouster, and gifted Russia a sanctions reprieve. Trump also hasn’t had much success brokering a ceasefire, much less an end to the war (an announced “energy ceasefire” fell apart-near instantly earlier in October). First Lady Melania Trump, however, has. She reportedly played a (limited) role in arranging a partial ceasefire for the frontline Ukrainian city of Oleshky, which has been hit especially hard by the war and is currently occupied by Russia. items.title: Patrick Stewart taught us what good men do with power
items.author: Ian Millhiser
items.summary: Patrick Stewart as Captain Jean-Luc Picard. | CBS via Getty Images When Patrick Stewart, who died on Wednesday, first stepped onto the bridge of the Enterprise in 1987 in his defining role as Captain Jean-Luc Picard, the Berlin Wall still stood. The Soviet Union would not fall until the fourth season of that show, Star Trek: The Next Generation, had already begun. Yet Picard’s generation of Star Trek franchise anticipated both events , portraying a post-Cold War world just as the Cold War was ending. It was the quintessential show for an age of American hegemony. For those unfamiliar with the franchise, Star Trek is primarily a story about Starfleet, which serves as both the military arm and as a kind of diplomatic corps for the United Federation of Planets, a benevolent, democratic union of more than a hundred worlds. In Star Trek’s Original Series, the 1960s episodes featuring Kirk and Spock, the Federation stands in the same shoes as the Cold War United States — vast and powerful, but also harried by other galactic superpowers like the Klingon Empire.
